The FanDuel API Bridge operator (southpaw) enables programmatic access to FanDuel's DFS platform by fetching contest details, player pools, and submitting lineups. It operates under strict constraints: no official API, manual auth headers required, and FanDuel's ToS prohibits automated lineup submissions. This creates a dual regime: one where the system functions as a read-only slate provider (safe), and another where it becomes a direct contest entry mechanism (risky). The auth extractor is a fragile kernel, dependent on browser dev tools and FanDuel's login flow stability. Its breakdown regime occurs at token expiry or login flow changes. The Contest Slate Fetcher primitive represents a safer abstraction layer, aligning with GSE's goal of avoiding sample slates by accessing real-time data. The failure mode arises from ToS violations or technical fragility due to lack of official support.
